literal: Hui then requested a private audience to speak on affairs and fully memorialized what he had heard, saying:
idiomatic: Hui then requested a private audience to speak on affairs and fully memorialized what he had heard, saying:

literal: "The former emperor moved the capital because the people were attached to their native soil; therefore he issued the edict of winter and summer dual residence—only to provisionally settle popular intent.
idiomatic: "The former emperor moved the capital because the people were attached to their native soil; therefore he issued the edict of winter and summer dual residence—only to provisionally settle popular intent.

literal: Those were words of the time—not truly the former emperor's deep intent.
idiomatic: Those were words of the time—not truly the former emperor's deep intent.

literal: Moreover in recent years the migrants have dwelt in peace many years; public and private plans are settled—there is no mind to return.
idiomatic: Moreover in recent years the migrants have dwelt in peace many years; public and private plans are settled—there is no mind to return.

literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to complete the enterprise the High Ancestor fixed—do not believe wicked ministers' words that it should not be so."
idiomatic: I humbly wish Your Majesty to complete the enterprise the High Ancestor fixed—do not believe wicked ministers' words that it should not be so."

literal: The emperor accepted it.
idiomatic: The emperor accepted it.

literal: Again promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Right Guard General.
idiomatic: Again promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Right Guard General.

literal: Though without supplementing benefit, he was deeply favored in intimacy.
idiomatic: Though without supplementing benefit, he was deeply favored in intimacy.

literal: Whatever confidential matters within the forbidden precincts—Hui separately received edicts and stored them in a chest; only Hui entering might open it; the rest of the attendants and yellow gates had no knowledge.
idiomatic: Whatever confidential matters within the forbidden precincts—Hui separately received edicts and stored them in a chest; only Hui entering might open it; the rest of the attendants and yellow gates had no knowledge.

literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Chang also received gracious favor; therefore men of the time called them "Starved Hawk General, Hungry Eagle Attendant."
idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Chang also received gracious favor; therefore men of the time called them "Starved Hawk General, Hungry Eagle Attendant."

literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

literal: Accepting bribes for office—all had fixed prices: great commanderies two thousand bolts, middle commanderies one thousand, lower five hundred; other offices each had differences; all under heaven called it the Market Bureau.
idiomatic: Accepting bribes for office—all had fixed prices: great commanderies two thousand bolts, middle commanderies one thousand, lower five hundred; other offices each had differences; all under heaven called it the Market Bureau.

literal: On leaving for the province he continuously loaded goods in carts; from Xindu to Tangyin the head and tail linked without break along the road.
idiomatic: On leaving for the province he continuously loaded goods in carts; from Xindu to Tangyin the head and tail linked without break along the road.

literal: When the carts lacked grease for horns, he met oxen on the road and freshly cut off horns to fill the need.
idiomatic: When the carts lacked grease for horns, he met oxen on the road and freshly cut off horns to fill the need.

literal: Hui inspected and mustered household registers, permitting return to chief registers; he issued a levy of fifty thousand bolts of silk.
idiomatic: Hui inspected and mustered household registers, permitting return to chief registers; he issued a levy of fifty thousand bolts of silk.

literal: Yet he amassed without limit—the people suffered.
idiomatic: Yet he amassed without limit—the people suffered.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming he was summoned as Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy; an edict made him act in Personnel selection affairs.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming he was summoned as Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy; an edict made him act in Personnel selection affairs.

literal: Later it was announced that Hui together with Prince of Rencheng Cheng, Prince of Jingzhao Yu, and Prince of Dongping Kuang would jointly decide great matters at the Gate Office.
idiomatic: Later it was announced that Hui together with Prince of Rencheng Cheng, Prince of Jingzhao Yu, and Prince of Dongping Kuang would jointly decide great matters at the Gate Office.

literal: Hui again submitted a memorial discussing essentials of government: the first said the censor's office must obtain worthy men—must obtain the right man, not bound by rank and grade; long in the matter, demand success.
idiomatic: Hui again submitted a memorial discussing essentials of government: the first said the censor's office must obtain worthy men—must obtain the right man, not bound by rank and grade; long in the matter, demand success.

literal: The second said pacify the people and secure the borders, observe the time and then act.
idiomatic: The second said pacify the people and secure the borders, observe the time and then act.

literal: In recent times border generals lack far-reaching strategy, greedy for one-in-ten-thousand merit; the good accord between Chu and Liang is unheard of, while the silkworm-woman's grievance is repeatedly tied—this is what petty men do, keen for treacherous profit.
idiomatic: In recent times border generals lack far-reaching strategy, greedy for one-in-ten-thousand merit; the good accord between Chu and Liang is unheard of, while the silkworm-woman's grievance is repeatedly tied—this is what petty men do, keen for treacherous profit.

literal: The plan to pacify Wu has its own good design—not in one city one garrison.
idiomatic: The plan to pacify Wu has its own good design—not in one city one garrison.

literal: Moreover several provinces of Hebei are the state's foundation; famine many years, households scattered in flight.
idiomatic: Moreover several provinces of Hebei are the state's foundation; famine many years, households scattered in flight.

literal: Now on the borders troops are again levied and sent—at a time like this, how easy to stir movement?
idiomatic: Now on the borders troops are again levied and sent—at a time like this, how easy to stir movement?

literal: I foolishly think that for several years past one should only quiet the borders to rest levies and summons, settle the people and encourage farming, show favor to central China.
idiomatic: I foolishly think that for several years past one should only quiet the borders to rest levies and summons, settle the people and encourage farming, show favor to central China.

literal: I request sternly to admonish border generals: from now on those in garrison whom bandits ask to submit within—do not permit rashly to send relief and receive; all must be reported to the throne.
idiomatic: I request sternly to admonish border generals: from now on those in garrison whom bandits ask to submit within—do not permit rashly to send relief and receive; all must be reported to the throne.

literal: Violators though they have merit, I request they be judged by violation of edict.
idiomatic: Violators though they have merit, I request they be judged by violation of edict.

literal: The third said the state's stores depend solely on Hebei.
idiomatic: The third said the state's stores depend solely on Hebei.

literal: Famine accumulated years, households fled and scattered; grown crafty and deceitful, thereby producing concealment.
idiomatic: Famine accumulated years, households fled and scattered; grown crafty and deceitful, thereby producing concealment.

literal: They shrink the old and young, falsely register death and loss, collect men's land tax and levy, and cut it into their own.
idiomatic: They shrink the old and young, falsely register death and loss, collect men's land tax and levy, and cut it into their own.

literal: The people are trapped below, the officials lose above.
idiomatic: The people are trapped below, the officials lose above.

literal: Unless one anew establishes authoritative regulations and well inspects and musters, the drain will come—from what is not yet ended.
idiomatic: Unless one anew establishes authoritative regulations and well inspects and musters, the drain will come—from what is not yet ended.

literal: I request deliberation on the matter, clearly proclaiming articles and regulations.
idiomatic: I request deliberation on the matter, clearly proclaiming articles and regulations.

literal: The emperor accepted it.
idiomatic: The emperor accepted it.

literal: Hui by nature loved literature; he gathered Confucian scholars Cui Hong and others to compile essentials of the hundred schools by category, titled Records by Subject, altogether two hundred seventy scrolls, rising from Fuxi down to Jin, fourteen generations in all.
idiomatic: Hui by nature loved literature; he gathered Confucian scholars Cui Hong and others to compile essentials of the hundred schools by category, titled Records by Subject, altogether two hundred seventy scrolls, rising from Fuxi down to Jin, fourteen generations in all.

literal: When Hui was gravely ill he memorialized and presented it.
idiomatic: When Hui was gravely ill he memorialized and presented it.

literal: He died; granted Eastern Garden secret vessels; posthumously Commissioner with staff, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, Duke of Works, posthumous title Wenxian.
idiomatic: He died; granted Eastern Garden secret vessels; posthumously Commissioner with staff, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, Duke of Works, posthumous title Wenxian.

literal: At the burial, given feather canopy, class sword, and twenty drummers and pipers, one hundred twenty guards of the feathered forest.
idiomatic: At the burial, given feather canopy, class sword, and twenty drummers and pipers, one hundred twenty guards of the feathered forest.

literal: Son Bi, styled Zongfu, was gentle and thick, with beautiful bearing.
idiomatic: Son Bi, styled Zongfu, was gentle and thick, with beautiful bearing.

literal: As the Zhuang Emperor's nephew by marriage, specially enfeoffed Viscount of Guangchuan.
idiomatic: As the Zhuang Emperor's nephew by marriage, specially enfeoffed Viscount of Guangchuan.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Secretariat.

literal: Bi's younger sister was taken by Emperor Xiaowu; because of kinship he was entrusted, courtesy exceptionally lofty.
idiomatic: Bi's younger sister was taken by Emperor Xiaowu; because of kinship he was entrusted, courtesy exceptionally lofty.

literal: He held posts of Supervisor of the Secretariat, Recorder of the Secretariat Affairs, specially advanced, and Clan Mentor.
idiomatic: He held posts of Supervisor of the Secretariat, Recorder of the Secretariat Affairs, specially advanced, and Clan Mentor.

literal: When Qi received the mandate he was made Left Grand Master of the Glorious Light.
idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate he was made Left Grand Master of the Glorious Light.

literal: In the third year of Tianbao he died.
idiomatic: In the third year of Tianbao he died.

literal: In the tenth year his sons together with all the Yuans were executed to death.
idiomatic: In the tenth year his sons together with all the Yuans were executed to death.

literal: Bi's younger brother's son Shijiang had clever invention.
idiomatic: Bi's younger brother's son Shijiang had clever invention.

literal: By the time of Qi Wucheng he was Director of Palace Construction.
idiomatic: By the time of Qi Wucheng he was Director of Palace Construction.

literal: De's younger brother Zan had quite a reputation, fond of stating military and state affairs.
idiomatic: De's younger brother Zan had quite a reputation, fond of stating military and state affairs.

literal: When the Office of the Province was first established, Zan was made Inspector and enfeoffed Marquis of Shanggu.
idiomatic: When the Office of the Province was first established, Zan was made Inspector and enfeoffed Marquis of Shanggu.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen admonished Zan to transform the capital region—he could proclaim filial conduct and must make customs harmonious and rites and decorum fully complete.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen admonished Zan to transform the capital region—he could proclaim filial conduct and must make customs harmonious and rites and decorum fully complete.

literal: From now on whoever is unfilial or unfraternal—compare at his gate, carve it on his pillar.
idiomatic: From now on whoever is unfilial or unfraternal—compare at his gate, carve it on his pillar.

literal: Again an edict said, "The Inspector of the Province—office lofty and position weighty, duties summing the capital region—selection belongs to worthy kin, to fulfill the hope of full gaze.
idiomatic: Again an edict said, "The Inspector of the Province—office lofty and position weighty, duties summing the capital region—selection belongs to worthy kin, to fulfill the hope of full gaze.

literal: But the princes are young and not versed in government substance—therefore it is given to Zan, that he may assist Hui in the Way and transformation.
idiomatic: But the princes are young and not versed in government substance—therefore it is given to Zan, that he may assist Hui in the Way and transformation.

literal: Now the Province is first established, commanderies and counties first set—dukes and ministers down all have their original affiliations; each may lead sons and younger brothers to extend mutual respect."
idiomatic: Now the Province is first established, commanderies and counties first set—dukes and ministers down all have their original affiliations; each may lead sons and younger brothers to extend mutual respect."

literal: Thereupon he was granted the name "Zan."
idiomatic: Thereupon he was granted the name "Zan."

literal: An edict made Zan ride the step-drawn carriage into the palace gate, added Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, transferred Left Deputy.
idiomatic: An edict made Zan ride the step-drawn carriage into the palace gate, added Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, transferred Left Deputy.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowen was about to plan moving the capital, the dukes mostly differed; only Zan approved the great plan.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen was about to plan moving the capital, the dukes mostly differed; only Zan approved the great plan.

literal: Each year when the emperor campaigned south he took his hand and entrusted later affairs.
idiomatic: Each year when the emperor campaigned south he took his hand and entrusted later affairs.

literal: He died; posthumously General of the Guard, Deputy as before.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously General of the Guard, Deputy as before.

literal: Later because of the merit of remaining behind and Zan's assisting, he was advanced to Earl of Jinyang.
idiomatic: Later because of the merit of remaining behind and Zan's assisting, he was advanced to Earl of Jinyang.

literal: Zan's younger brother Shu, styled Mairen.
idiomatic: Zan's younger brother Shu, styled Mairen.

literal: He bent the bow three hundred jin and was skilled at mounted archery.
idiomatic: He bent the bow three hundred jin and was skilled at mounted archery.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was Administrator of Hedong.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was Administrator of Hedong.

literal: Hedong custom had many merchants and few tilled the mulberry and grain—even unto thirty years without knowing plow and hoe.
idiomatic: Hedong custom had many merchants and few tilled the mulberry and grain—even unto thirty years without knowing plow and hoe.

literal: Shu on taking office encouraged farming; he personally went to teach and show; within two years every household had enough, men had enough—for this a song was made:
idiomatic: Shu on taking office encouraged farming; he personally went to teach and show; within two years every household had enough, men had enough—for this a song was made:

literal: "In Taizhou's Hedong, shuttles replace pounding; when Lord Yuan arrived, the fields at last were ordered."
idiomatic: "In Taizhou's Hedong, shuttles replace pounding; when Lord Yuan arrived, the fields at last were ordered."

literal: He died as General of Pingcheng Garrison, posthumous title Jing.
idiomatic: He died as General of Pingcheng Garrison, posthumous title Jing.

literal: He had seven sons.
idiomatic: He had seven sons.

literal: Jihai styled Yuanquan—among brothers the most renowned, post Inspector of Luo Province.
idiomatic: Jihai styled Yuanquan—among brothers the most renowned, post Inspector of Luo Province.

literal: Jihai's wife was the daughter of Minister of Works Li Chong, the Zhuang Emperor's maternal aunt, granted title Lady of Tang commandery.
idiomatic: Jihai's wife was the daughter of Minister of Works Li Chong, the Zhuang Emperor's maternal aunt, granted title Lady of Tang commandery.

literal: Power lay with Erzhu; calamity was just beginning—she urged Jihai to take an outer post to avoid the slightest entanglement.
idiomatic: Power lay with Erzhu; calamity was just beginning—she urged Jihai to take an outer post to avoid the slightest entanglement.

literal: At the Zhuang Emperor's calamity Jihai indeed because he was in the frontier was spared.
idiomatic: At the Zhuang Emperor's calamity Jihai indeed because he was in the frontier was spared.

literal: Following Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong he was enfeoffed Prince of Fengyi, post Minister of the Secretariat and Inspector of Yong Province, transferred Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Following Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong he was enfeoffed Prince of Fengyi, post Minister of the Secretariat and Inspector of Yong Province, transferred Minister of Works.

literal: He died of illness; posthumous title Mu.
idiomatic: He died of illness; posthumous title Mu.

literal: Son Heng, styled Deliang, also named Xiaocai.
idiomatic: Son Heng, styled Deliang, also named Xiaocai.

literal: Meeting Zhou and Qi's partition, he was several years old; with his mother Lady Li he was in Luoyang.
idiomatic: Meeting Zhou and Qi's partition, he was several years old; with his mother Lady Li he was in Luoyang.

literal: Qi Shenwu because Heng's father was in Guanzhong confined him.
idiomatic: Qi Shenwu because Heng's father was in Guanzhong confined him.

literal: His mother then claimed cold and hunger, obtained to go eat at Tangyin, entrusted to the great magnate Li Changshou, and brought Heng and several orphaned nephews to reach Chang'an.
idiomatic: His mother then claimed cold and hunger, obtained to go eat at Tangyin, entrusted to the great magnate Li Changshou, and brought Heng and several orphaned nephews to reach Chang'an.

literal: Zhou Wen as a meritorious minister's son greatly honored him.
idiomatic: Zhou Wen as a meritorious minister's son greatly honored him.

literal: At the end of Datong he inherited the title Prince of Fengyi, repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Xun Province, changed to Prince of Pingliang.
idiomatic: At the end of Datong he inherited the title Prince of Fengyi, repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Xun Province, changed to Prince of Pingliang.

literal: When Zhou received the mandate, by precedent he was demoted to duke.
idiomatic: When Zhou received the mandate, by precedent he was demoted to duke.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the mandate, from Inspector of Luo Province he was summoned as Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the mandate, from Inspector of Luo Province he was summoned as Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

literal: Soon he went out as Inspector of Wei Province; in office eight years, transformation was greatly harmonized.
idiomatic: Soon he went out as Inspector of Wei Province; in office eight years, transformation was greatly harmonized.

literal: Because of old age and illness he begged bones; officials and people went to the gate and memorialized to retain him; the emperor sighed long at it.
idiomatic: Because of old age and illness he begged bones; officials and people went to the gate and memorialized to retain him; the emperor sighed long at it.

literal: That year Heng because of grave illness again requested return to the capital; the emperor ordered envoys to bring medicine and inquire after his condition—envoys met one another on the road.
idiomatic: That year Heng because of grave illness again requested return to the capital; the emperor ordered envoys to bring medicine and inquire after his condition—envoys met one another on the road.

literal: He died at home; posthumous title Xuan.
idiomatic: He died at home; posthumous title Xuan.

literal: Prince of Chenliu Qian, son of Gegen.
idiomatic: Prince of Chenliu Qian, son of Gegen.

literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he was enfeoffed Duke of Chenliu.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Dengguo he was enfeoffed Duke of Chenliu.

literal: With Prince of Wei Yi he broke the Qufo tribe; he followed in attacking Wei Chen.
idiomatic: With Prince of Wei Yi he broke the Qufo tribe; he followed in attacking Wei Chen.

literal: When Murong Bao came to raid, Qian cut off his left wing and Bao was defeated.
idiomatic: When Murong Bao came to raid, Qian cut off his left wing and Bao was defeated.

literal: Murong Chui in rage and resentment came to Sanggan; Qian was brave yet treated the enemy lightly; in battle at Chen he fell.
idiomatic: Murong Chui in rage and resentment came to Sanggan; Qian was brave yet treated the enemy lightly; in battle at Chen he fell.

literal: Qian's bearing was towering and his martial strength unmatched; because his spears were fine and short he made large ones, yet still fretted they were light and again hung bells on the blade below.
idiomatic: Qian's bearing was towering and his martial strength unmatched; because his spears were fine and short he made large ones, yet still fretted they were light and again hung bells on the blade below.

literal: His bow strength was double that of ordinary men.
idiomatic: His bow strength was double that of ordinary men.

literal: Because of these singularities the armory of the capital always kept them and recorded them.
idiomatic: Because of these singularities the armory of the capital always kept them and recorded them.

literal: Qian often speared a man and, piercing through, held him aloft.
idiomatic: Qian often speared a man and, piercing through, held him aloft.

literal: Again he once with one hand planted his spear in the ground, feigned retreat on horseback; enemies vied to seize it but could not draw it out.
idiomatic: Again he once with one hand planted his spear in the ground, feigned retreat on horseback; enemies vied to seize it but could not draw it out.

literal: Qian drew his bow and shot—one arrow killed two or three men; those who tugged the spear lost their souls and scattered; he slowly had men take the spear and left.
idiomatic: Qian drew his bow and shot—one arrow killed two or three men; those who tugged the spear lost their souls and scattered; he slowly had men take the spear and left.

literal: Each time he followed campaigns and as partial general he was always first to scale and break the line—brave foremost in the age; enemies without regard to numbers dared not resist those before him.
idiomatic: Each time he followed campaigns and as partial general he was always first to scale and break the line—brave foremost in the age; enemies without regard to numbers dared not resist those before him.

literal: When he died.
idiomatic: When he died.
